problem: Existing spatial-reasoning benchmarks for MLLMs end at offline QA/grounding and do not test whether inferred spatial context guides closed-loop action. Existing navigation benchmarks (VLN, goal-oriented) confound spatial reasoning with instruction following and model-dependent exploration.
motivation: Embodied agents must carry spatial knowledge from prior visual experience (e.g. a tour video) into later decisions. A benchmark is needed that gives scene context as a fixed prior video, so failures can be attributed to destination resolution versus closed-loop navigation.
key_idea: Video-contextualized navigation: give the agent a prior indoor tour video and a video-grounded instruction (Count/Order/Distance/Orientation room-to-object or Instance object goals), with navigation as the primary task and goal identification as a diagnostic probe.
insight: Goal identification correlates strongly with navigation success, but a large gap remains: MV-DualVLN reaches 43.1% Rid-SR versus 31.7% RSR, and 62.2% of correctly identified episodes still fail. Ablations show the full prior video matters (target-frame-only drops SR 27.6 to 19.7). Shuffling video frames or reversing relations in the instruction causes large drops, so the model really uses temporal and relational structure. Distance and Orientation are the hardest types.
method: Benchmark construction: MP3D floor-level tour videos from a genetic-algorithm traversal of the nav graph, spline-smoothed with randomized camera and lighting; sliding-window prior videos; template instructions rephrased by Gemini-3.1 Flash; duplicate/short (<3m) episodes filtered; manual validation of all test episodes.
Five instruction types: Instance (object goal) and Count, Order, Distance, Orientation (room-to-object goals), covering entity-grounded, trajectory-structured and geometry-aware reasoning.

Evaluation protocol: navigation with SR (within 1m of any valid viewpoint), SPL and a relaxed Room SR (RSR); diagnostic goal identification (pick the prior-video frame matching the destination) scored by Rid-SR / Oid-SR.

MV-DualVLN baseline: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct fine-tuned (frozen vision encoder) from DualVLN System 2. Inputs are the prior video (50 frames), nav history, and 4-view observations. It first selects a target frame, then predicts a pixel goal and a stop signal, executed by an oracle executor.
Feature pooling: 384x384 images, 12x12 features pooled to 3x3 (16x fewer tokens) for the prior video and history.
Training data: pixel goals derived from frontiers closest to the target on a running occupancy map; stop is true within 3m geodesic of the target.
Baselines: hierarchical (Gemini-3 or oracle frame + MTU3D) and end-to-end (3D-Mem zero-shot and fine-tuned, Uni-Navid).

setting.training_data: VCN-Bench train set: 61 MP3D scenes, 309 tour videos, 103,055 episodes
setting.observation: prior RGB video (50 frames) plus 4-view (front/left/back/right) RGB at the current and initial positions; depth and pose available to the agent
setting.action_space: pixel-space waypoint goals executed by an oracle executor; underlying actions FORWARD 0.25m / TURN 30° / STOP, 1000-step limit
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scans, Hello Robot Stretch agent)
setting.privileged: oracle low-level executor for waypoints; the Oracle+MTU3D variant uses GT target frames

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,250 test episodes on 11 unseen MP3D scenes
numbers.extra: oracle executor for waypoints; prior video downsampled to 50 frames
oracle executor; own fine-tuned variant of an existing method
ground-truth target frame given as goal-frame prefix (oracle analysis)

numbers_note: Baseline rows are excluded. Goal-identification results for proprietary and open MLLMs are baselines, not the paper's method. MV-DualVLN Gid: average Rid-SR 43.1, Oid-SR 49.6 (text).
results: The best model, MV-DualVLN, achieves 27.6 SR, 19.1 SPL and 33.9 RSR, above fine-tuned 3D-Mem (18.1 SR) and Gemini-3+MTU3D (17.6 SR). Zero-shot baselines score below 9 SR. In goal identification, the best MLLM (Qwen3.8-Flash) reaches 54.2 Rid-SR against 89.6 for humans.
limitations: Static MP3D scenes: the scene is assumed unchanged between the prior-video and navigation phases, and the prior video fully covers start and goal.
Limited coverage of proprietary MLLMs (API cost and frame limits); an oracle executor factors out low-level control.
Matterport3D is mostly Western-style indoor scenes, which biases the benchmark.
